search_strategy: Chat: full per-channel dumps via the Mattermost API (all 11 channels, ~9800 messages total) to /tmp/chat/<channel>.txt, then targeted `grep -rn -i` for specific keyword sets ('sentinel'; 'interleave|adopt_ledger|num_cached|turn_ledger.py|TurnEntry|TurnLedger'; 'END_OF_CONVERSATION') plus date-range `sed -n` reads of clusters the greps pointed at. This found essentially everything with a distinctive shared vocabulary but missed remarks phrased with terms outside the chosen keyword sets (e.g. say21's 'read_sidecar', l1's 'jsonl replay', l8's 'created'/'verified' pairing) even though the raw channel text was sitting on disk the whole time. Wiki: enumerated ALL ~168 pages via the BookStack API with comment counts, then bulk-dumped body+comments for pages matching a second round of greps ('responses_0|seed_message|multiturn|agent') into /tmp/wiki/<id>.txt. Every page it explicitly opened it read whole, including comments (140, 139, 143, 147, 150, 152) — correctly distinguishing real requirement comments from decoy page bodies twice (page 144's turn_ledger.json/jsonl scheme, page 143's budget_exhausted/agent_signal/error/cancelled scheme). But page 211 (the one page holding 3 of the corpus's remarks, including the ONLY occurrence of the literal constant name TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME) was only ever matched by a file-listing grep and its title header via `head` — its body and comments were never displayed, a genuine search-vs-open gap rather than a keyword-coverage gap. Mail: single full IMAP dump to /tmp/mail.txt via imaplib, then every one of the 8 relevant threads was read in full — 8/8 mail remarks found, the strongest-covered surface. Truncation from the terminal's screen-buffer limits (repeated '[horizon watchdog]' stalls, `head`/`tail`/`sed -n` windows) cut off page 144's one comment right after its decoy body was fully read, and generally forced narrow slice reads rather than full-file cats for the largest channels (#engineering, #code-review, #pipeline, each 2000+ messages).
notable: The two failure modes behind g7.r1's 0.0 are independent and both diagnosable in the transcript: a naming slip (TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME vs shipped SIDECAR_FILENAME, line 9496) caused by never opening wiki page 211, and a reasoning slip (created vs adopted status on a missing sidecar) caused by misreading fix27's 'freshly built ledger, status created' as describing verify_sidecar's OUTPUT rather than its INPUT, stated explicitly by the agent at line 3565 and again at line 5681.
